title: Distributed Rate Limiter
question: Design a scalable distributed rate limiter service to protect an API gateway handling 100,000 requests per second. How would you architect this?

rubric.name: requirements_clarification
rubric.description: Clarifies throughput (RPS), algorithm rules (token bucket vs sliding window log), client identification (IP vs User ID), and response handling (HTTP 429).

rubric.name: high_level_architecture
rubric.description: Proposes API gateway middleware with centralized cache (e.g. Redis cluster) and atomic operations.

rubric.name: data_storage_decisions
rubric.description: Selects in-memory storage (Redis) with Lua scripting or sliding window counters to eliminate race conditions.

rubric.name: scalability_reliability
rubric.description: Addresses distributed race conditions, cache cluster sharding, replication, and fail-open vs fail-close trade-offs.

rubric.name: observability_tradeoffs
rubric.description: Discusses metrics, alert thresholds, latency overhead, and gracefully handling Redis outage.

expected_signals: Compares algorithms (Token Bucket, Leaky Bucket, Fixed Window, Sliding Window Counter)
Identifies race conditions in multi-threaded/distributed rate limit checks and uses Redis Lua script / INCR
Explicitly chooses fail-open (allow traffic with warning) vs fail-close (block traffic) policy during storage downtime
red_flags: Stores rate limit counters in relational disk DB (e.g. Postgres) introducing prohibitive read/write disk latency
Ignores race conditions between read-and-update counter steps
Fails to specify client identifier or location of rate limiter (client vs gateway vs app server)
follow_up_prompts: What happens when the central Redis cluster experiences a network partition? Would you fail open or fail closed?
How would you prevent hot keys when a single viral user generates millions of requests?
